 WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (CBS12) — A frozen smoked salmon product distributed in Florida is being recalled over possible Listeria contamination, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
 Krasnyi Oktyabr Inc., a New York-based wholesale distributor, voluntarily recalled Starfish Seafood Premium Cold Smoked Norwegian Salmon Sliced in 8-ounce packages. The FDA published the recall notice Oct. 16.
 No illnesses have been reported, according to the FDA.
 See also: Florida mom vanishes after 'People’s Court’ appearance; ex-fiancé arrested 14 years later 
 The recalled product can be identified by:
 Brand: Starfish Seafood
 Size: 8 ounces (227 grams)
 UPC: 4751048940099
 Lot: D080-148
 Best-by date: Nov. 27, 2027
 The frozen salmon was distributed in Florida, New York, Georgia, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Ohio.
 The potential contamination was discovered through product sampling by the New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets, according to the FDA.
 Listeria can cause serious illness, particularly in young children, older adults, people with weakened immune systems, and pregnant women. Infection during pregnancy can cause miscarriage or stillbirth.
 Consumers should not eat the recalled salmon and should return it to the place of purchase for a full refund.
 Questions can be directed to Krasnyi Oktyabr Inc. at (718) 858-6720, Monday through Friday, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern time.
